name: Downtown Boise
tagline: The core, the greenbelt and the coworking
description: The compact centre around 8th Street and the Basque Block, with the restaurants, the breweries, the capitol and most of the city's coworking. The Boise River greenbelt runs along its southern edge and the foothill trailheads are a short ride north.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to work and live without driving
pros: Genuinely walkable with the best food and bars
cons: The most expensive rents in the city
Quiet on weeknights compared with larger cities

name: North End
description: The historic residential district north of downtown, bungalows and craftsman houses on streets of mature trees, with Hyde Park as its small commercial centre. Camel's Back Park and the Ridge to Rivers trailheads are at the top of the neighbourhood.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting character and trail access on foot
pros: The most attractive housing in Boise
cons: Expensive and rarely available to rent
Twenty minutes on foot to downtown

name: Boise Bench
tagline: The plateau south of downtown, cheaper and mixed
description: The elevated area south of the river, historically working class and now the most affordable part of the city with a view back over downtown. Vista Avenue and Orchard Street carry a genuinely good run of Mexican, Basque and Vietnamese food.
bestFor: Budget stays with a short ride into the centre
pros: Considerably cheaper than downtown or the North End
The best cheap food in Boise
Views over the city and quick access to the greenbelt
cons: Less walkable, most errands need a car
Housing stock is older and mixed quality
Airport flight path over parts of it

name: Garden City
tagline: The riverside strip turned artist quarter
description: A separate municipality wedged along the river northwest of downtown, historically industrial and now holding studios, breweries, cideries and the Surel's Place arts residency. The greenbelt runs through it and rents remain below the city proper.
bestFor: Anyone wanting studio space, breweries and the river path
pros: Growing cluster of studios and taprooms

name: Southeast Boise
tagline: The university side, along the river
description: The area east of Boise State along the river, with the campus, newer apartment blocks, Bown Crossing's small commercial centre and the longest continuous stretch of greenbelt. It is quieter than downtown and cycling into the centre takes fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Cyclists and anyone wanting river access with newer housing
pros: The best greenbelt access in the city
Fifteen minutes to downtown by bike
cons: Less character than the older districts
